title: SLO Alignment & Capacity Negotiation Procedure
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This runbook describes the operational process for aligning product-level SLO decisions with capacity commitments and error budget negotiations. It is intended for SREs, product managers, and platform engineers who must make binding capacity and rollout decisions that affect cost, latency, and availability.

When to use:
- Quarterly capacity planning and SLO review cycles.
- Prior to any model rollout, large feature launch, or forecasted traffic spike (marketing campaigns, integrations).
- During emergency error-budget burns when capacity scaling/contract changes are required.

Primary owners and stakeholders:
- SRE lead (primary): Martin Cho
- Platform capacity owner: Priya Nair
- Product/PM liaison: Elena Rodriguez
- Finance lead for compute commitments: Caleb Morris
- Customer-impact escalation: Customer Success oncall

Definitions and guardrails:
- SLOs: formal service-level objectives for user-visible metrics. Typical Redwood inference SLOs:
  - Latency SLO (P99): <= 150 ms for hosted-small (interactive) tier
  - Availability SLO: 99.95% successful request rate (5xx + throttles excluded where appropriate)
  - Embedding throughput SLO: >= 400 req/s per dedicated pool per 16xA100 equivalent (example baseline)
- Error budget: 1 - SLO (e.g., 0.05% allowed unavailability per month for 99.95% SLO).
- Capacity headroom: operational spare capacity to cover unexpected surges; baseline is 20% of forecasted steady-state by default.

High-level process overview:
1) Forecast & telemetry review (SRE + Product + Finance)
2) Map SLOs to capacity requirements (per-route modeling)
3) Negotiate headroom and cost tradeoffs (Finance + Product + SRE)
4) Commit to reserved capacity or autoscale policies (Platform + SRE)
5) Instrument and create a short-lived canary with strict error-budget monitoring
6) Post-rollout review and lessons learned (80/20 RCA + capacity reconciliation)

Detailed procedure:
A. Forecast & telemetry review (2–3 weeks before commit)
- Inputs: rolling 90-day telemetry (qps, tokens/req, request size distribution) from Prometheus/Grafana and sample traces from Jaeger.
- Action items:
  1. SRE exports the following time series for the past 90 days:
     - request_qps_total{route}
     - tokens_per_request{route}
     - latency_p50,p95,p99{route}
     - 5xx_rate{route}
  2. Product provides expected growth multiplier and event dates.
  3. Finance provides cost targets (monthly GPU $/hour budget or committed spend limits).
- Deliverable: a capacity forecast spreadsheet with 3 columns: conservative (95th), expected (median), optimistic (10th).

B. Map SLOs to capacity (per-route model)
- Use per-route performance profiles (see runtime profiling catalog). For each route:
  - Estimate token/s demand = qps * avg_tokens_per_request
  - Estimate tokens/s supply per GPU = baseline_throughput_tokens_per_gpu(route_profile) * (efficiency_factor)
  - GPUs_required = ceil((tokens/s demand) / (tokens/s supply per GPU))
- Example calculation (steady-state):
  | Route | qps | avg_tokens | tokens/sec | tokens/sec/GPU | GPUs req | note |
  | Production inference | 120 | 32 | 3840 | 120000 | 1 (baseline; but apply buffer) | baseline model small-8k context |
  - Apply headroom: GPUs_committed = ceil(GPUs_req * (1 + headroom_percent)). Default headroom_percent = 20%.

C. Negotiation rubric (SRE + Product + Finance)
- Error-budget policy triggers negotiation when projected monthly error-budget burn > 10% extra compared to baseline.
- Tradeoffs to present:
  - Increase reserved capacity (commit) to reduce P99 latency risk and lower on-demand costs.
  - Use aggressive batching/quantization suggestions from Redwood Optimize to lower tokens/sec per GPU.
  - Adjust SLO targets for non-critical routes (e.g., lower SLO from 99.95% to 99.9% for background rerankers).
- Negotiation outcome options:
  1. Commitment to n extra GPUs for the quarter (Finance approval)
  2. Deploy autoscale policy with temporary burst buffer up to m GPUs (cost caps + alerts)
  3. Accept a controlled SLO change for non-critical traffic with documented customer-facing notice

D. Commit & operationalize
- Platform must create capacity tickets in the capacity tracker and schedule provisioning windows.
- Config checklist:
  - Reserve pool label: "commit-Q4-2026-{team}"
  - Autoscale policy: min_gpus = committed_gpus, max_gpus = committed_gpus + burst_limit
  - Cost caps: billing_alert_threshold = (monthly_spend_budget * 0.9)
- Example Git patch (redwoodctl):
  redwoodctl capacity reserve --pool commit-Q4-2026-ml --gpus 8 --min 8 --max 12 --owner @platform

E. Canary and early-warning instrumentation (first 48 hours)
- Create ephemeral canary with 5% of traffic or 1–2 replica models depending on sensitivity.
- Dashboards to watch (Grafana):
  - "SLO Overview - Production" (top card: P99 latency, error rate, traffic by route)
  - "Capacity Utilization - GPU Pools" (utilization, queue length, tokens/sec per GPU)
- Prometheus alerting rules to add/verify:
  - slo_error_budget_burn_rate{service=\"inference\"} > 8 over 1h -> P2 notify SRE
  - gpu_pool_utilization > 85% for 10m -> P1 notify SRE + platform
  - request_latency_bucket{le=\"0.15\"} < 0.99 (for P99) -> warning
- Immediate actions if canary triggers:
  1. Pause rollout and scale up committed pool by +1 GPU (if available).
  2. Open temporary traffic diversion to a fallback model variant (lower quality) if latency or 5xx rises above threshold.

F. Post-rollout reconciliation (within 7 days)
- Run an 80/20 RCA focused on capacity assumptions and telemetry mismatches.
- Update the per-route performance catalog with observed tokens/sec per GPU and tail-latency profiles.
- Finance reconciles actual spend vs forecast and issues adjustments for next planning cycle.

Incident review standards (brief):
- Any incident where SLO loss > 0.5% or where error-budget consumed > 25% in 24 hours requires an "SLO Incident Review". This review must include:
  - Timeline of mitigation steps with timestamps.
  - Capacity decisions made and why (provisioning delays, autoscale limits, config errors).
  - Action items with owners and deadlines (fixes, capacity purchase, telemetry gaps).
- Evidence artifacts: Grafana panel snapshots, alert history, redwoodctl capacity events, cost spike logs.

Operational tooling references and queries:
- Prometheus example queries:
  - P99 latency (route): histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"inference\"}[5m])) by (le,route))
  - Error budget burn: increase(slo_error_budget_spent_total{service=\"inference\"}[1d]) / increase(slo_error_budget_total{service=\"inference\"}[1d])
  - GPU utilization: avg(gpu_utilization_percent) by (pool)"
